Find the probability of detecting it in \(0\leq x\leq L/2\).
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Probability and the Born Interpretation under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Apply equation [3]. The wavefunction is real, so \( |\psi|^2=(2/L)\sin^2(\pi x/L)\). Use \(\sin^2 y=(1-\cos 2y)/2\): \[P=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^{L/2}\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right)\,dx=\frac{1}{L}\int_0^{L/2}\left[1-\cos\left(\frac{2\pi x}{L}\right)\right]\,dx.\] Integrating each term gives \[P=\frac{1}{L}\left[x-\frac{L}{2\pi}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi x}{L}\right)\right]_0^{L/2}=\frac{1}{L}\left(\frac{L}{2}-0\right)=\frac12.\] Final result: \(\boxed{P(0\leq x\leq L/2)=1/2}\), consistent with the density's symmetry about \(L/2\).

Final answer:
\(\boxed{P(0\leq x\leq L/2)=1/2}\), consistent with the density's symmetry about \(L/2\).
